description: Planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude, height above the Mars reference sphere. Used for catalogue positions and for the HiRISE DTMs.

radiusM.note: A_AXIS_RADIUS = 3396.19 km in both HiRISE DTM labels.

description: CORRECTED_X / CORRECTED_Y of MERB_traverse_5130.csv. Stage 2 tests (scripts/mars/fit_traverse.py, fit_victoria.py): the sol-1 row is exactly (0, 0); the rover leaves the 27 m Eagle-crater DTM grid on sol 57 (NASA: exit 22 Mar 2004); rows lie inside the Endurance DTM grid on sols 94-319; on Victoria's rim 2,104 drives fit a circle of 410.1 m radius against the DTM's 408.7 m rim crest (scale correct to 0.3%). So: metres east/north of the landing site. ABSOLUTE registration is unresolved: the Victoria centre lands 316-335 m from where the published landing coordinates put it, explainable by a ~2.8 deg rotation or a ~300 m origin offset; one tie point cannot separate them (needs an Endeavour tie).
axes: x east, y north, metres from the rover position on sol 1 (landing site)

origin.note: The two published landing coordinates differ by ~125 m, and neither reproduces the Victoria tie (316-335 m residual). Not usable for absolute placement until a second tie is fitted.

description: Local metric grid of the Eagle and Endurance crater DTMs from the traverse page's osu/ folder (producer not named on the page) (header: MAP_UNITS meters, PROJECTION_NAME Unknown). Eagle spans x −13…14 m, y −13…14 m; Endurance x 667.7…834.8 m, y −43.2…−219.4 m — consistent with a landing-site-centred east/north grid, but the axes and origin are not stated, so it is recorded as unknown.
